commit.message:
docs: fix broken SEP-2133 link in SEP-2640 (#3439)

* docs: fix broken SEP-2133 link in SEP-2640

Every "SEP-2133" link on the SEP-2640 page pointed at the relative URL
"Extensions" and returned a 404 on the docs site.

The References entry `- [SEP-2133]: Extensions` is valid link reference
definition syntax (label, colon, single word). Markdown uses the first
definition it finds, so that list item overrode the real definition at
the end of the file and disappeared from the rendered list.

Write the SEP entries in the References list as collapsed reference
links (`[SEP-N][]`), which cannot be read as definitions, and regenerate
docs/seps. The SEP-2549 and SEP-2076 entries render exactly as before.

* docs: regenerate SEP index and redirects

The generated SEP index is out of date on main, so `npm run check:seps`
(the render-seps CI job) fails for every pull request that touches SEPs.

SEP-2127 (MCP Server Cards) was added without re-running
`npm run generate:seps`. docs/docs.json is missing the /seps/2127
redirect, and docs/seps/index.mdx still counts 42 Final SEPs instead
of 43.

This is the unedited output of `npm run generate:seps`.

Merge main into docs/progressive-disclosure-wg-charter

Resolve the navigation conflict by retaining the Scientific Computing interest group while removing the renamed Primitive Grouping entry. Preserve the approved Progressive Disclosure charter, navigation, redirect, and Skills Over MCP references, along with all upstream changes.

docs: serve the TypeScript quickstart server with serveStdio (#3427)

* docs: serve the TypeScript quickstart server with serveStdio

The 2026-07-28 "Build an MCP server" quickstart wired its TypeScript
server with `server.connect(new StdioServerTransport())`, which only
serves clients that open with the 2025-era `initialize` handshake. A
server built from the page failed version negotiation against
2026-07-28 clients, while the Inspector's default `legacy` era hid the
failure.

Build the server in a `createServer()` factory and serve it with
`serveStdio(createServer)` from `@modelcontextprotocol/server/stdio`,
which negotiates the era per connection and keeps 2025-era clients
working. Explain why the factory returns a fresh instance, note that the
hand-wired form only serves 2025-era clients, and add an Inspector CLI
step that lists the tools in the `modern` era. The draft copy of the
page receives the same change.

Fixes #3422

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XFU2zyusVTttWcakgCjXjR

* docs: say when serveStdio calls the quickstart's createServer factory

The comment above createServer said serveStdio calls it once per
connection. The SDK calls the factory for every instance it needs, which
is twice when a server/discover probe is followed by an initialize
fallback, as the paragraph under "Running the server" already says.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01XFU2zyusVTttWcakgCjXjR
